name: Cascaded recovery: virgin share after several recovery stages
summary: Computes the share of a material stream that must still come from virgin material after a series of recovery stages, its proven lower bound, and how much the cascade beats the best single stage.

lean.verification_receipt_id: jdhart81/viridis-research runs/2026-11-16_P3 P3.CascadedRecovery (statement a4e3f3c269b8, candidate eaafbaaa17a7)

inputs.name: recovery_fractions
inputs.help: Share of the material reaching each stage that the stage recovers, from 0 to 1, in stream order.

hypotheses.statement: Every stage recovers a nonnegative fraction (no stage adds demand).
No stage recovers more than reaches it.

scope: A single material stream passing through recovery stages in series, each recovering a fixed fraction of what reaches it.
boundary: Exact arithmetic of the series-stage model only. It does not establish any real recovery rate, losses between stages, quality downgrades, rebound demand, or that the stages are independent; it is not empirical validation, Viridis review, certification, a credit, or a registry determination.

provenance.statement_text: For every n and every r : Fin n -> R with 0 <= r i <= 1, the virgin share prod(1 - r i) satisfies: (1) 0 <= share <= 1; (2) for every m with r i <= m <= 1, (1 - m)^n <= share, in particular (1 - max r)^n <= share; (3) for every stage j, share <= 1 - r j; (4) if r j < 1 and some other stage k != j has r k > 0, then share < 1 - r j.

statement_conformance.statement: (1 - m)^n <= virgin share for every uniform bound m with max r <= m <= 1; the reported lower bound is (1 - max r)^n
statement_conformance.check: approx_eq(uniform_lower_bound, pow(1 - sorted(recovery_fractions)[-1], len(recovery_fractions))) and approx_le(uniform_lower_bound, virgin_share) and all(approx_le(pow(1 - m, len(recovery_fractions)), virgin_share) for m in [sorted(recovery_fractions)[-1], (sorted(recovery_fractions)[-1] + 1) / 2, 1])

statement_conformance.statement: virgin share <= 1 - r j for every stage j (never worse than any one stage)
statement_conformance.check: all(approx_le(virgin_share, 1 - r) for r in recovery_fractions) and approx_eq(best_single_stage_share, 1 - sorted(recovery_fractions)[-1]) and approx_le(virgin_share, best_single_stage_share)

statement_conformance.statement: virgin share < 1 - r j whenever r j < 1 and another stage k != j has r k > 0
statement_conformance.check: all((virgin_share < 1 - recovery_fractions[j]) if (recovery_fractions[j] < 1 and any((recovery_fractions[k] > 0) if k != j else False for k in range(len(recovery_fractions)))) else True for j in range(len(recovery_fractions))) and cascade_strictly_better == ((1 - best_single_stage_share) < 1 and any((recovery_fractions[k] > 0) if k != best_single_stage else False for k in range(len(recovery_fractions))))

statement_conformance.statement: virgin share = prod(1 - r i); recovered share = 1 - virgin share; gain = best single-stage share - virgin share
statement_conformance.check: approx_eq(virgin_share, prod([1 - r for r in recovery_fractions])) and approx_eq(recovered_share, 1 - virgin_share) and approx_eq(cascade_gain, best_single_stage_share - virgin_share) and stage_count == len(recovery_fractions)

provenance.lean_witnesses: [1/2,1/2] -> 1/4 (strictly below 1/2); [1/2,1/4,0] -> 3/8 above (1/2)^3; controls [0,1/2] and [1/2,1] meet the single stage exactly; r = 2 and r = -1 are refused.
